newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus rises on Telepiu hopes.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus rises on Telepiu hopes.

text.p: Shares in French pay television group Canal Plus were four percent higher on Tuesday, building on strong recent gains on expectations the group will get control of Telepiu in Italy.

The Canal Plus board is set to meet on Wednesday and could agree a deal with German media groups Bertelsmann and Kirch under which the French group would swap its stake in German pay television group Premiere for Kirch's stake in Telepiu and a cash payment.
Les Echos newspaper recently suggested the cash payment could be as much as two billion francs ($340 million).

At 1427 GMT, Canal Plus was up 4.11 percent at 1,191 francs, having risen from 997 francs on June 2. Company officials said on June 27 during the annual meeting that they were in talks with the German groups to exchange its 37.5 percent stake in Premiere for Kirch's 45 percent stake in Telepiu. Canal Plus already has 45 percent in Telepiu since its merger with Nethold.
Carlo Campomagnani, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said he was reiterating his positive stance on Canal Plus despite the recent rally, saying the price was "still far from the full value."
